title: Risk Management and Homefield Recovery
summary: IMSAFE, CRM, see-and-avoid principles, and visual straight-in recovery fundamentals.
overview: This event shifts attention from pure aircraft handling to the human and procedural factors that shape safe contact-phase flying. You will review IMSAFE, CRM, and visual collision avoidance while also briefing a homefield visual straight-in and the flight profile that ties the local area back into a standardized recovery at NAS Corpus Christi.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items
studyNotes.summary: The common thread is discipline before the maneuver ever starts: check the pilot, check the crew, check the environment, and then fly a recovery profile that stays predictable for everyone else in the system.

items.text: IMSAFE stands for illness, medication, stress, alcohol, fatigue, and eating, and it is the first risk-management check in every brief.
If an SNA is not fit to fly, the process includes notifying the IP, going to the ODO, and completing the appropriate IMSAFE paperwork and medical referral if required.
IMSAFE is not a loophole for poor planning. It is a safety tool that applies to any syllabus event, not just flights.
CRM is the use of behavioral skills to reduce preventable crew error and optimize risk management.
Core ideas emphasized in this event include:
SNAs still need to perform as if single-piloted even when an IP is present. Good CRM does not replace aircraft control; it supports it.
See and avoid remains the primary defense against midair collisions, especially in VMC near airports.

children.text: Accommodation delay when shifting focus outside.
A narrow focus zone and blossom effect.
Reduced detection from haze, glare, or dirty windscreens.

items.text: Use disciplined scan patterns and TCAS support, but do not substitute electronics for actually looking outside.
From SHAMROCK, the visual straight-in begins by slowing to 200 KIAS and requesting the straight-in with the tower.

children.text: Descend to 800 feet MSL for south flow or 500 feet MSL for north flow.
Configure below 150 KIAS with gear down and flaps as required.
Intercept the extended centerline and make the correct base or final gear-down report.

items.text: This recovery only works well if you enter stabilized and stay ahead of the configuration timeline.
